chunks: The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) informed us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammam, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who converted to Islam in
the middle of the month of Ramadan, what is incumbent upon him regarding fasting? He said: There is not incumbent upon him except what he converted to Islam in.
ai.seo_question: What is the fasting obligation for someone who converts to Islam during Ramadan?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a new convert (*mu'allaf*) is exempt from making up the days of Ramadan prior to their conversion, as the obligation of fasting begins only upon the acceptance of Islam. This ruling highlights the principle that religious duties are incumbent from the moment of entry into the faith, distinguishing between the obligation of *qada'* (making up) and the immediate duty of *ada'* (performance). It underscores the mercy and practicality in Shia jurisprudence regarding the gradual integration of new Muslims into the community's ritual practices.
